title: Blister packaging, behind-the-counter placement and direct delivery of scheduled listed chemical products
subtopic: Packaging, placement and delivery at retail
rule_summary: Under 21 CFR 1314.05 and 21 U.S.C. 830(d)(2), a regulated seller or mail order distributor may not sell a scheduled listed chemical product in nonliquid form (including gel caps) unless the product is packaged either in blister packs, with each blister containing no more than two dosage units or, if blister packs are technically infeasible, in unit dose packets or pouches. Under 21 CFR 1314.25 and 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(A)(i), (ii) and (ix)(I), each regulated seller must ensure that sales of a scheduled listed chemical product at retail are made in accordance with 1314.25 and 1314.20; must place the product so that customers do not have direct access to the product before the sale is made (behind-the-counter placement), a placement that includes circumstances in which the product is stored in a locked cabinet that is located in an area of the facility where customers do have direct access; and must deliver the product directly into the custody of the purchaser. Mobile retail vendors must place the product in a locked cabinet.
exam_relevance: Tests the physical conditions of a lawful retail sale that apply apart from the logbook: blister or unit-dose packaging for nonliquid forms, no direct customer access before the sale, the locked-cabinet form of behind-the-counter placement, and delivery directly into the purchaser's custody.

authority.name: Requirements regarding packaging of nonliquid forms
Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum dosage units in each blister
numeric_facts.conditions: Nonliquid forms, including gel caps, packaged in blister packs

exceptions: Where blister packs are technically infeasible, a nonliquid form may be packaged in unit dose packets or pouches.
Behind-the-counter placement includes storing the product in a locked cabinet located in an area of the facility where customers do have direct access.
common_confusions: An open shelf or display that customers can reach before the sale is not behind-the-counter placement, even when it stands inside or beside the pharmacy department.
The packaging requirement is stated for nonliquid forms, including gel caps.
verification_notes: 21 CFR 1314.05 and 1314.25 read in the eCFR, current through 2026-09-14, with their currency confirmed on 2026-09-16; 21 U.S.C. 830(d)(2) and (e)(1)(A) read in the Office of the Law Revision Counsel's online United States Code on 2026-09-16.
